sources.citation: Oldendorp, C. G. A. (ed. J. J. Bossart). 1777. C. G. A. Oldendorps Geschichte der Mission der evangelischen Brüder auf den caraibischen Inseln S. Thomas, S. Croix und S. Jan. Erster Theil. Barby. Book III §8 "Sprachen der Neger", pp. 344-346 + folding numeral/noun table; Wawu ethnography pp. 288-289.
sources.note: Nothing. This is the primary attestation: p. 345 gives two 'Wawu' translations of one sentence; the second, 'Anders: Christus esoaree, amboaree anjembo' (verified on the page image), plus the numeral row 'Anders: baba, bauli, janna, tofla, guena, brong...' and the nouns 'Wawu: Gajiwodu. Varriadad...' in the table, are the Wawu-II material. p. 288-289 note that the Wawu 'nicht durchgängig einerley Sprache redet' (two speakers, one from the interior, one from near the coast) and list the coastal speaker's neighbours Fra, Bente, Naena, Gui, Gurraa, Guaflee, No. No remark on pronunciation, accent…
